row.evidence: BombBomb's pricing page lists "SSO (SCIM / Okta)" only under Enterprise ("Custom teams pricing"), and the Okta SCIM help article says "Plan Type: Enterprise".
row.notes: New row. Core $36 and Core + Copilot $56 per user/mo billed annually ($42/$70 monthly); Enterprise is custom-priced and carries SSO and SCIM. SSO is Okta OIDC or SAML 2.0 (Entra, OneLogin, JumpCloud and others), set up by BombBomb support. SCIM: Okta Integration Network app (OAuth 'Authenticate with BombBomb') and an Entra non-gallery app pointed at https://api.bombbomb.com/v2/scim with an admin's OAuth token copied from the BBV2APITOKEN browser cookie. Okta deactivation marks members deactivated and lowers the seat count; group push to subteams is not supported and email changes do not sync. Pricing page and the plan matrix put 'Open API access' on Enterprise only, but the API help articles list Core, Core + Copilot and Enterprise (see conflicts). Category set to Sales & CRM because BombBomb is sold as video messaging for sales and relationship teams.

auth.token_source: Entra: the Paid Seat Team Admin's BombBomb OAuth token (BBV2APITOKEN cookie from app.bombbomb.com). Okta OIN app: OAuth consent via 'Authenticate with BombBomb'.

operations.notes: Update is documented as a capability (profile fields sync) without saying PUT or PATCH. Read is implied by Okta's 'Import existing users'.

deprovision.data_retained: Deactivated member keeps a restricted account: cannot sign in with Okta SSO, and after a password reset only a limited account without emails, videos or contacts. Admin-side deactivation keeps videos and data in the workspace. Self Paid users are removed from the team; invited users have the invitation revoked.

core: addresses (street, city, state, postal code, country)
attributes.notes: Docs list friendly field names, not SCIM attribute paths; mapped here to the nearest SCIM core attribute. Entra list says 'Job title' and 'Phone number' and omits Organization.

limitations.text: Email address changes in the IdP are not synced to BombBomb.
Okta groups cannot be synced to BombBomb subteams; Entra group provisioning must be disabled.
Provisioning is queued and can take up to 30 minutes.
Only Team Admin or Super Admin can set up Okta provisioning.

capabilities.notes: Team members can be listed, added, updated and removed from a team; subteams can be created and deleted. GET /user returns only the caller's own info. No documented deactivate endpoint.

endpoints.purpose: Remove a member from a team

limitations.text: One API key per account; only Admins and Application Admins can generate it.

okta.notes: OIN page marks OIDC, SWA, SCIM and Create, Update, Deactivate as checked (read from page markup); Group Push not checked. BombBomb's own help article documents the OIN SCIM setup.

entra.notes: No Microsoft Learn tutorial for BombBomb in the Entra SaaS app index. BombBomb documents a non-gallery Entra app for both SAML and SCIM and says older gallery templates are not supported.

onelogin.notes: BombBomb's SAML article names OneLogin as a supported SAML provider; no OneLogin SCIM guide found.

jumpcloud.notes: jumpcloud.com/support/integrate-with-bombbomb returns AccessDenied (no guide). BombBomb's SAML article names JumpCloud as a SAML provider.

conflicts.text: The pricing page and the 'What's Included in Each Plan' matrix put 'Open API access' on Enterprise only, while the API help articles say the API applies to Core, Core + Copilot and Enterprise. user_api_plan follows the pricing page.
Okta's catalogue page says the OIDC app supports just-in-time provisioning, but BombBomb's SAML article says users must exist in both BombBomb and the SSO provider. fallbacks.jit left null.

open_questions: SCIM version is not stated (the tenant URL is /v2/scim, where v2 is BombBomb's API version).
Docs do not say whether SCIM deactivation ends active sessions, or whether DELETE is supported.
Whether PUT or PATCH is used for updates, and whether filtering/pagination are supported, is undocumented.
SCIM and API rate limits are not published.
No audit-log API or user-event webhooks are documented (webhooks cover contacts).
Google Workspace and OneLogin catalogue listings not checked (OneLogin blocks bots).
